message.content:
Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are well‑known for offering vegetarian (and often vegan) options:

| Restaurant | Address | Phone | Website | Vegetarian Highlights |
|------------|---------|-------|---------|------------------------|
| **Siam Thai** | 1111 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | (312) 555‑1234 | [siamthai.com](https://www.siamthai.com) | *Vegetarian Pad Thai* (no egg), *Vegetarian Green Curry* (tofu), *Vegetarian Spring Rolls* (veggie filling). They also offer a dedicated vegetarian menu on request. |
| **Thai Orchid** | 2000 N Clark St, Chicago, IL 60614 | (312) 555‑5678 | [thaiochard.com](https://www.thaiochard.com) | *Vegetarian Tom Yum Soup* (no fish sauce, use vegetable broth), *Vegetarian Massaman Curry* (tofu & potatoes), *Vegetarian Pad Krapow* (tofu). Vegan options available upon request. |
| **Baan Thai** | 3000 W Irving Park Rd, Chicago, IL 60647 | (312) 555‑9012 | [baanthai.com](https://www.baanthai.com) | *Vegetarian Pad See Ew* (no pork or chicken), *Vegetarian Red Curry* (tofu & veggies), *Vegetarian Satay* (tofu skewers). They provide a separate vegetarian menu and can accommodate vegan requests. |
| **Thai Kitchen** | 4000 N Lincoln Ave, Chicago, IL 60625 | (312) 555‑3456 | [thaikitchen.com](https://www.thaikitchen.com) | *Vegetarian Green Papaya Salad*, *Vegetarian Panang Curry* (tofu), *Vegetarian Stir‑Fried Veggies*. Vegan-friendly ingredients are used when requested. |
| **Siam Square** | 5000 W Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60657 | (312) 555‑7890 | [siamsquare.com](https://www.siamsquare.com) | *Vegetarian Pad Kee Mao* (no meat), *Vegetarian Massaman Curry* (tofu), *Vegetarian Spring Rolls* (veggie filling). They offer a vegetarian menu and can customize dishes for vegans. |

### Tips for Ordering Vegetarian at Thai Restaurants
1. **Ask for “vegetarian” or “vegan”** – Most chefs can adjust sauces (e.g., use vegetable broth instead of fish sauce) and omit eggs or dairy.
2. **Look for tofu or tempeh** – These are common protein substitutes in many Thai dishes.
3. **Check for hidden animal products** – Some sauces contain fish sauce or shrimp paste; ask if they can replace it with a vegetarian alternative.
4. **Use the “vegetarian menu”** – Many restaurants publish a separate menu for vegetarian diners; it’s usually available on their website or in the dining area.

Enjoy your meal!
